themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged to 6 this week compared to a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 4,700% spike (z-score: 17.76)—suggesting a sudden, coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in Central Harlem this week.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 17.76)
4,700% increase is the single largest statistical anomaly in the dataset
No prior Reddit or news coverage explaining the spike
reporting_angles: Are illegal posters targeting specific corridors (e.g., subway entrances, commercial strips on 125th Street)?
Interview 311 operators or NYPD enforcement unit: Is there a known poster group, or did enforcement lapse?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Illegal Posting Convergence
themes_detail.summary: Both graffiti (6 complaints this week vs. 0.8 weekly average, +700%) and illegal posting (+4,700%) spiked simultaneously this week, suggesting coordinated street degradation in Central Harlem requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: Graffiti complaints: 6 this week vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.04, +700%)
Illegal posting complaints: 6 this week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 17.76, +4,700%)
Both complaints peaked in the same week, suggesting a coordinated street campaign
reporting_angles: Walk key corridors (125th Street, Frederick Douglass Boulevard, Amsterdam Avenue) and photograph graffiti patterns and illegal posters to identify targets or messages.
Contact Parks Dept and NYPD Sanitation Enforcement for evidence of organized activity or gang-related graffiti.

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 8 last week vs. a 0.5 weekly average—a 1,500% spike (z-score: 7.5)—indicating either a sudden crackdown on street vendors or a new cluster of unlicensed vending operations in Central Harlem.
evidence: 8 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.5, +1,500%)
Second-largest spike in the dataset; suggests sudden policy shift or vendor population change
No concurrent news coverage explaining the spike
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and the Street Vendors Project: Is the city suddenly enforcing licenses, or have unlicensed vendors proliferated?
Check with NYC Department of Consumer Affairs (DCWP) for recent enforcement actions or licensing changes affecting Central Harlem.

themes_detail.label: Sanitation System Under Stress
themes_detail.summary: Missed waste collection jumped to 11 complaints last week vs. a 2.4 weekly average (+363%, z-score: 5.22), while unsanitary conditions remain elevated at 1,289 complaints over 90 days, indicating a possible sanitation crew shortage or scheduling breakdown this week in Central Harlem.
evidence: Missed collection complaints: 11 this week vs. 2.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.22, +363%)
Unsanitary condition complaints: 1,289 total over 90 days (second-highest complaint category)
Spike is acute and new, suggesting a recent service disruption rather than chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation: Are there crew absences, vehicle breakdowns, or route changes in Central Harlem this week?
Walk residential blocks and document uncollected trash; interview residents on how long collection has been missed.

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints peaked at 33 three weeks ago vs. a 15.8 weekly average (+110%, z-score: 5.22), coinciding with missed collection surge, indicating potential rodent population growth tied to sanitation gaps in Central Harlem.
evidence: Rodent complaints: 33 three weeks ago vs. 15.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.22, +110%)
Temporal overlap with missed collection spike suggests sanitation failure driving rodent problem
Rodent complaints remained elevated for multiple weeks, indicating a sustained issue
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) on rodent activity in Central Harlem; request latest complaint and inspection data.
Talk to residents and building managers about rodent sightings, entry points, and whether pest control services have been deployed.
